title: Enterprise Onboarding: Health Checks, QBR, Integration & Escalation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
## Purpose
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended process for enterprise customer onboarding, integration checklist, escalation procedures, known issues and workarounds, and quarterly health/QBR materials. Intended audience: Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and Product/Platform owners.

## Quick summary / scope
- Applies to enterprise customers (Dedicated, Private, or hybrid deployments) during onboarding and the first 6\u201312 months of production use.
- Covers: pre-onboard checklist, week-by-week onboarding milestones, API & network integration guidance, escalation matrix (sev definitions, owners, SLAs), common known issues and mitigations, health-checks dashboard and a QBR agenda/template.

## Table of contents
1) Ownership and SLAs
2) Pre-Onboarding checklist
3) 90-day onboarding milestones (week-by-week)
4) Integration guide (network, API, webhooks)
5) Escalation playbook (sev matrix & run steps)
6) Known issues & workarounds
7) Health checks & QBR materials
8) References and related runbooks

---

## 1) Ownership and SLAs
- Primary owner: Customer Success (assigned CSM).
- Technical owner: Solutions Engineering / Support (named SE & Support lead per account).
- Product/Engineering escalation: Eng on-call (pager) for Sev 1/2, Product PM for regressions impacting quality.
- Standard support expectations for enterprise customers: initial response within 1 business hour for Sev 1, 4 hours for Sev 2, 1 business day for Sev 3, 3 business days for Sev 4.
- Contractual SLA (if applicable): follow the customer's support tier in contract; map our internal Sev -> contractual priority.

### Ownership table
| Area | Role | Default Owner | Contact |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Onboarding project lead | Manager | CSM | csm+<account>@redwood.ai |
| Integration / API questions | Technical SE | Solutions Engineer | se+<account>@redwood.ai |
| Escalation to eng | Incident commander | Support Lead / Eng on-call | support@redwood.ai + PagerDuty |

## 2) Pre-Onboarding checklist (To be completed before Kickoff call)
- Signed contract, PO, or purchase confirmation.
- Legal & security questionnaires completed (if private/dedicated: complete security handoff checklist).
- Account provisioning: API key created, test project initialized in Redwood Console, billing configured.
- Network prep (for Private/VPC): customer provides IP ranges, firewall rule list, and VPN details.
- Sample dataset and acceptance criteria for initial quality checks.
- Kickoff meeting scheduled with CSM, SE, customer engineering, and procurement (if needed).

## 3) 90-day onboarding milestones (recommended)
Phase: Week 0 (Kickoff)
- Agenda: Introductions, success criteria, timeline, key contacts.
- Deliverables: Project plan in shared workspace, initial access & credentials, start environment smoke test.

Phase: Weeks 1\u20132 (Integration & smoke testing)
- SE pairs with customer to integrate SDK/API. Verify token auth, model selection, and sample prompts.
- Validate network connectivity (for private/dedicated): ping, TLS validation, certificate exchange.
- Deliverable: Integration sign-off checklist.

Phase: Weeks 3\u20136 (Workload validation & performance tuning)
- Run representative workload, capture latency/throughput, and token cost.
- Apply batching/cache/quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize.
- Deliverable: Performance baseline report and config recommendations.

Phase: Weeks 7\u201312 (Stabilization & rollout)
- Integrate fallbacks and canary rollout policy (per product docs).
- Finalize runbook handoff, SLO definitions, alerting thresholds in customer\u2019s monitoring.
- Deliverable: Production readiness checklist & go-live sign-off.

## 4) Integration guide (API, network, webhooks)
### API basics
- Base URL (hosted): https://api.redwood.ai/v1
- Auth: Bearer token in header: Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
- Example cURL: 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}]}'

### Network requirements
| Component | Required ports | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hosted API | 443 (HTTPS) | Allow outbound TLS to api.redwood.ai and region-specific endpoints |
| Dedicated / Private | 443, 22 (admin only), VPN ports | Customer to open inbound rules for support-maintained endpoints after approval |

### Webhooks & callbacks
- Recommend: use a stable HTTPS endpoint that supports TLS 1.2+.
- Retry policy: Redwood will retry webhook delivery 3 times with exponential backoff (5s, 20s, 60s).
- Signature: X-Redwood-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256). Verify using your webhook secret.

### Sample webhook validation (pseudocode)
- Compute HMAC-SHA256 of request body with webhook secret; compare to header. Reject if mismatch.

## 5) Escalation playbook
### Severity definitions
- Sev 1 (Critical): Platform unavailable for customer or data loss. Customer business-critical flows blocked. Target initial response: 1 hour. Target remediation or workaround: 4 hours (or agreed contractual target).
- Sev 2 (High): Major degradation impacting important flows (high latency, partial functionality). Initial response: 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Functional but non-critical issues (errors on edge cases). Initial response: 1 business day.
- Sev 4 (Low): Minor bugs, feature requests. Initial response: 3 business days.

### Escalation steps (ordered)
1. Triage by Support Engineer: validate, collect logs, replication steps.
2. If reproducible and Sev >= 2, escalate to Support Lead and open an incident in PagerDuty.
3. If code-level or infra needed, pager Eng on-call and notify Product PM.
4. Communicate status to customer within SLA window; include temporary workaround if available.
5. Post-incident: run blameless postmortem if Sev 1 or recurring Sev 2.

### Escalation matrix (contact & timings)
| Severity | Initial owner | Escalation target | Response SLA | Pager | Email alias |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| Sev 1 | Support Engineer | Support Lead -> Eng on-call -> Product PM | 1 hour | Yes | sev1@redwood.ai |
| Sev 2 | Support Engineer | Support Lead -> Eng on-call | 4 hours | Conditional | sev2@redwood.ai |
| Sev 3 | Support Engineer | Support Lead | 1 business day | No | sev3@redwood.ai |
| Sev 4 | Support Engineer | CSM backlog | 3 business days | No | support@redwood.ai |

### Incident response checklist (for Support Engineer)
1. Collect: request ID, customer org ID, request timestamps, sample payloads, region, model/version.
2. Reproduce: run same prompt and parameters in sandbox.
3. Escalate: follow matrix above with required artifacts.
4. Mitigate: apply temporary fallback (older model, different route) if available.
5. Communicate: status update every 60\u2013120 minutes for Sev 1; every 4\u20138 hours for Sev 2.

## 6) Known issues & workarounds (living table)
| ID | Symptom | Root cause (short) | Workaround | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| KI-2025-001 | Excessive latency spikes during long-context chat | KV cache thrashing under bursty prefix distribution | Reduce sequence length in prompt or enable prefix caching; apply recommended batching policy | monitoring |
| KI-2025-007 | Occasional "invalid token" errors on rotating keys | Short TTL on client-side caching + clock skew | Ensure clients refresh tokens using provided refresh endpoint; sync NTP on clients | resolved |
| KI-2026-013 | Webhook signature mismatch errors for some customers | Proxy rewrites body (Content-Encoding) before HMAC validation | Instruct customers to configure proxy to preserve raw body or use Redwood SDK helper that verifies signature after proxy | investigating |

Notes: keep this table up-to-date. Add a new row for each customer-impacting pattern and tag with statuses: monitoring / investigating / resolved / workaround_pushed.

## 7) Health checks & QBR materials
### Recommended dashboards & metrics (minimum set)
- Latency (p50/p95/p99) by model & route (goal: p95 < 300ms for low-latency tiers).
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) by route and model (goal: < 0.5% 5xx).
- Throughput (tokens/sec) and cost per 1K tokens by model.
- Cache hit ratio (prefix/KV) \u2014 target > 65% for steady workloads.
- Autoscale events and CPU/GPU utilization for Dedicated customers.
- Customer-specific request distribution (top prompt templates).

### Health check runbook (weekly)
1. Run smoke tests against customer endpoints (sample prompts).
2. Validate p95 latency and error rate thresholds; alert if breached.
3. Check billing anomalies (sudden jump in token usage).
4. Review new known-issues hits correlated to customer logs.
5. Send weekly health summary to customer stakeholders.

### QBR template (quarterly)
- Attendees: CSM, SE, Customer Eng Lead, Product PM (as needed).
- Duration: 60\u201390 minutes.
- Agenda:
  1) Executive summary (CSM): adoption, any critical incidents, overall health.
  2) Key metrics (SE): latency, error rate, cost per 1K tokens, cache hit ratio, top API routes.
  3) Usage patterns and growth plan (Customer)
  4) Roadmap alignment & feature requests (Product)
  5) Action items and timelines (owner + ETA)
- Deliverables: QBR slide deck, action tracker, updated runbook.

#### QBR slide checklist
- Cover slide: customer name, quarter, date, participants.
- Metrics: charts for p95 latency, 5xx rate, tokens/day.
- Reliability review: incidents since last QBR, RCA status.
- Optimization opportunities: model/quantization recommendations, caching strategy.
- Risks & next steps.

## Appendix: Templates
- Integration sign-off checklist (copy into customer doc):
  - API key created and rotated test passed
  - Sample requests returned expected shapes (examples attached)
  - Webhook signature verified in staging
  - Network connectivity validated (TLS and IP rules)
  - Cost baseline established

- Incident communication template (email to customers):
  Subject: [Redwood] Incident update - <short description>
  Body: Summary, impact, current status, mitigation steps, ETA for next update, contact.
